STEREO VRS (NVIDIA, EXPERIMENTAL) — 0.2.0

Select Stereo VRS in the launcher. This uses native OpenXR stereo; QVFR and
VectorXR are not required. A compatible NVIDIA GPU and NVAPI driver are required
for coarse shading. Other hardware continues rendering ordinary full-rate stereo.
Check diagnostics for nv_vrs ready / world_vrs counters, not just the selector.

Auto uses XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction when the active runtime exposes it. Missing,
inactive, invalid or offscreen gaze falls back to the fixed region for that frame.
Fixed skips gaze input. Focus width/height are percentages of each projected eye
image; positive offsets move right/up. The region remains inside the image.
Shading rates: 1x1 is the control; 2x2 reduces peripheral shader work; 4x4 is more
aggressive and may visibly degrade peripheral detail. Intersecting 16-pixel tiles
remain full rate. This is shading-rate reduction, not higher-resolution focus.

VRS keeps the original two eye draws and adds no focus scene traversals. Only
verified world-sort scopes use coarse shading. UI/shadows/unverified passes keep
normal shading. Runtime resolution and native in-game crop remain in effect;
quad-only resolution/crop/blur controls are disabled for this mode.

Benchmark overlay and recording remain available. Focus dimensions are zero in
VRS because no separate focus images exist. Compare matched scene, pose, runtime
resolution and image quality after warmup. No measured LMU speedup is promised.
CPU upload experiments remain Quad Views-only. Known conflicting QVFR/VectorXR/
OpenXR Toolkit layers are disabled only for this launched game process. Do not
combine with another VRS injector or driver-forced VRSS.

Late-attaching OpenXR input applications are not a generic compatibility target:
this layer is pinned to LMU. It adds its gaze action to normal app attachment;
for LMU without action sets it privately attaches at first locate. OpenXR permits
one attachment per session. No stored gaze history is written.

All 0.1.2 features remain available in their applicable modes. Native single-pass
stereo is unfinished and is not a 0.2.0 feature. Restart LMU to change render mode.

VALIDATION SCOPE
Native/WARP, fake OpenXR, gaze/projection and launcher/DPI suites pass with the
LLVM-MinGW build. A real NVIDIA D3D11 probe verified moving full-rate focus,
2x2/4x4 peripheral shading, the 1x1 control and state restoration. Ten consecutive
final-production probe processes exited cleanly after dynamic-map updates.
LMU/Pimax logs confirmed gaze input and VRS initialization in an earlier live
run. These checks establish implementation behavior, not a measured LMU speedup
or broad headset/image-quality compatibility. A matched awake-headset A/B
benchmark is still required before making performance claims.


NVIDIA VRS hardware check (0.5.2+)
----------------------------------
Close LMU and run tools\check-hardware-vrs.cmd. It needs no game or headset.
Result code 0 means: VRS reduces pixel shading on this GPU, per-eye shading-rate
maps apply correctly, a steady focus causes no re-upload, and the normal 1x1
shading is restored afterwards. The log is written to
tools\hardware-vrs-check.log.
